A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DADM study and contain the complete main paper, references and six-page supplement. Text and rendered-page comparison supports reliable assessment of all material.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-dataset experiments and ablations in Tables A-H, plus supplementary hyperparameter experiments and convergence results in Tables I-J and Figure 7.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results in the main paper and supplement, including Tables A-J and Figure 7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and supplementary Algorithm 1 retain the same ViT architecture, MIM and CDC-Adapters, MI-guided ReGrad, dual-alignment objectives, PG-IRM optimization and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both use CASIA-CeFA, PADISI-USC, CASIA-SURF and WMCA with RGB, depth and infrared. Protocols 1-4 retain the same fixed-modality, missing-modality, flexible-modality and limited-source-domain scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding Tables A-D, including CLIP and FLIP in Table A and MMDG and VP-FAS throughout. Tables E-H also retain the same component, loss, adapter and mask alternatives.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1-4.3 retain the same splits, HTER/AUC metrics, missing-modality handling and 0.3 missing probability. ViT-B/16, 224-by-224 inputs, 50 training epochs, Adam and batch size 32 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Component and design ablations in Tables E-H, supplementary hyperparameter sweeps in Tables I-J, and convergence, feature-distribution and attention-map analyses in Figures 5-9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: The cosine-similarity mean and standard-deviation displays in Figures 5 and 8 are identical. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings in Tables A-J and Figures 5-9 match. For example, Table A reports DADM averages of 13.63% HTER and 92.96% AUC in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical content is unchanged, including Section 3's objectives and supplementary Sections 6 and 9's Donsker-Varadhan, PG-IRM and angle-alignment statements, assumptions, derivations and proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the same contributions concerning MIM-based modality weighting, dual alignment and generalization, and state-of-the-art performance across four protocols. The conclusion's altered line wrapping does not change its claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality reliability and dual alignment are unchanged. Supplementary Sections 7 and 10 retain the same overfitting explanation and qualification that poorer transfer in two sub-protocols may reflect stronger domain shifts.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces 'The codes will be released soon' with 'Our code is available at here' and adds a repository hyperlink. Other reproducibility details are unchanged; repository contents and usability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning relative to MMDG and other prior approaches, and all 89 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: Minor text edits update the abstract's code-access sentence and the arXiv version/date stamp. Section order and other wording, including the conclusion, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The conclusion on page 9 has different spacing and line wrapping, and page 1 gains a colored code hyperlink. Figures, tables and Algorithm 1 retain their appearance and placement.

improvement.justification: The new repository hyperlink replaces a promised future release with a concrete code-access pointer, modestly improving reproducibility information. Scientific content and evidence are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
